summary: This agreement outlines the partnership between i-Escrow and 2TheMart, with the purpose of creating a co-branded escrow service. The key obligations of each party include providing content for the co-branded site, adhering to trademark usage policies, and ensuring compliance with California Escrow Law. Financial terms specify that 2TheMart will receive 0.025% of the average transaction size as advertising payments, while i-Escrow retains all rights to its intellectual property. The agreement has a one-year term, renewable for successive one-year periods upon mutual written agreement. Termination can occur due to breach, change in company structure, or bankruptcy, with either party providing written notice.

summary: Xencor, Inc. and Aimmune have entered into an agreement to collaborate on the development and commercialization of a product containing an antibody. The purpose of this agreement is to enable Aimmune to develop and commercialize the product in various countries, while Xencor retains rights to the antibody. Key obligations include Aimmune's responsibility for conducting Development Activities and Commercializing the product, as well as its obligation to make milestone payments to Xencor totaling $480,000. In return, Xencor grants Aimmune a license to use the antibody in the development and commercialization of the product. The agreement has a term of several years and may be terminated by either party upon certain conditions, including failure to meet milestones or breach of contract.

summary: The purpose of the agreement is to establish a partnership between ARCA U.S. TREASURY FUND and ARCA CAPITAL MANAGEMENT, LLC for the provision of blockchain administration services. The parties involved are ARCA U.S. TREASURY FUND, represented by Philip Liu as President, and ARCA CAPITAL MANAGEMENT, LLC, represented by J. Rayne Steinberg as Chief Executive Officer. Key obligations include the Blockchain Administrator's duties to perform its responsibilities under the agreement, including maintaining confidentiality of all information provided by the Fund. The Fund shall pay a fee calculated at an annual rate of 0.20% of its average annual net assets, accrued daily and paid monthly in arrears. The agreement may be terminated upon 60 days' written notice by either party or by vote of the Fund's Trustees or majority of outstanding voting securities.

summary: This contract outlines the terms of a research and development agreement between Howmedica Osteonics Corp and Conformis. The purpose is to develop a new product, referred to as the KIB Product, pursuant to a research and development plan. Conformis will furnish Deliverables to Stryker, which will analyze and test them for acceptance. Stryker may reject Deliverables that infringe on third-party intellectual property rights or do not meet specified criteria. If rejected, Conformis has a certain period to correct and redeliver the Deliverable. The financial terms include payments of $2,000,000 and $3,000,000. Termination is possible if Stryker properly rejects three or more Deliverables or if Conformis fails to deliver corrected versions within specified periods.

summary: National CineMedia, LLC and Network Affiliate have entered into an agreement to provide digital content services to the latter's theaters. The purpose of the agreement is to equip the theaters with necessary equipment for delivering digital content services. National CineMedia will install non-digital slide projectors in some theaters, acquire small d equipment for others, and allow Network Affiliate to purchase or lease Big D equipment. Network Affiliate will be responsible for obtaining consents required for installation and use of equipment at each theater. The costs associated with the use of equipment, including electricity and telephone lines, will be borne exclusively by Network Affiliate. National CineMedia will own the small d equipment it purchases, while Network Affiliate will own the Big D equipment. The capital costs of equipping new theaters to receive the service will be mutually agreed upon.

summary: About.com, Inc and Ebix have entered into an agreement to create and maintain the Insurance Center on About's website. The purpose of this partnership is to provide online insurance services to About's users. Key obligations include About creating and maintaining links to the Insurance Center, hosting the center within an About wrapper, and delivering a minimum number of Advertising Impressions and Filled Application Forms per Quarter. Ebix will pay About $480,000 in consideration for the Advertising Impressions, as well as fees for each Filled Application Form submitted through the Insurance Center. The agreement has a term of thirty months from the Effective Date, during which time Ebix is the exclusive integrated online insurance provider on certain channels and guide sites. Termination of the agreement will result in About's obligation to deliver only a pro-rated number of impressions and forms.

summary: Time Warner and Integrity Music have entered into a music publishing agreement to produce and distribute the "Integrity Music" series. The purpose of this agreement is to create a joint venture between the two parties to develop and market music products, including sound recordings and printed materials. Time Warner will be responsible for manufacturing and distributing the products, while Integrity Music will handle the creative aspects, including selecting artists and songs. The financial terms of the agreement include royalties paid by both parties on sales of the products, with Time Warner paying $1995 per unit sold in the United States and 75% of net receipts outside the US. Integrity Music will pay a royalty rate of $1795 per unit sold in the US and 7% of its net receipts outside the US. The agreement has a term of five years, ending on December 31, 2004, after which it can be extended with mutual written consent.

summary: VerticalNet, Inc. and LeadersOnline have entered into an agreement to provide job placement services through the VerticalNet website. The purpose of this agreement is to enable LeadersOnline to access the Resume Bank, a database of candidates seeking employment opportunities, and to display Employer Spotlights on the VerticalNet site. In exchange for these services, LeadersOnline will pay VerticalNet slotting fees for the Employer Spotlights, Banner and Newsletter Ad sponsorship fees, and a license fee for access to the Resume Bank. Additionally, LeadersOnline will pay VerticalNet 50% of its revenue generated from clients who utilize the LeadersOnline Services through the VerticalNet site. The agreement has a term of one year, after which it may be terminated by either party with written notice.

summary: Liquidmetal Technologies Inc. and Eutectix have entered into an agreement to collaborate on the development and production of metallic glass products. The purpose of this agreement is to enable Eutectix to manufacture Licensed Products using Liquidmetal's patented technology, while also providing access to Liquidmetal's technical information and equipment. Key obligations for Eutectix include maintaining the licensed equipment in good working order, complying with all reasonable directions from Liquidmetal, and paying a cash royalty of 6.0% on the invoice price of any Licensed Products sold by Eutectix or its permitted sublicensees. In return, Eutectix will have access to Liquidmetal's technical information and equipment, as well as the ability to manufacture Licensed Products for sale to third parties. The agreement has a term of three years, after which it may be terminated with prior written notice from either party.

summary: This Co-Branding Agreement, effective January 21, 2003, is between Lucent Technologies Inc. and mPhase Technologies Inc. The purpose of the agreement is to permit mPhase to use the Lucent Technologies name and logo on its multi-access product, subject to certain guidelines and conditions. Key obligations include mPhase's requirement to abide by co-branding guidelines, maintain the quality of its goods associated with the Lucent Co-Branding Logo, and allow Lucent to inspect approved uses bearing the logo. Lucent reserves the right to terminate the agreement in the event of a significant change in mPhase's management or ownership, bankruptcy proceedings against mPhase, or if mPhase fails to maintain product quality. The agreement shall continue for one year, with annual renewal options subject to Lucent's written consent. Upon termination, mPhase must immediately cease use of the Lucent Co-Branding Logo, except on goods sold prior to termination. Neither party is liable for special, incidental, or consequential damages.

summary: Marine MP, LLC has entered into a contract with MusclePharm to endorse their products. The agreement's purpose is to promote MusclePharm's business and products through Arnold Schwarzenegger's Name and Appearance Rights. Marine MP, LLC will provide four personal appearances in the first year, two appearances each in subsequent years, and participate in the production of a GetSwole training video. They will also supply signed items for promotional use. In return, MusclePharm will pay Marine MP, LLC 10% of Net Sales from the sale of certain products and promotional items. The agreement has a term of three years, with an option to extend. Termination can occur upon written notice by either party. Financial terms include $20 million in payments, 25% allocation for pension and health benefits, and 10% of Net Sales from product sales and promotional items.

summary: This agreement between VerticalNet, Inc and Neoforma outlines the terms of their partnership. The purpose is to establish a comprehensive online marketplace for medical products, with both parties contributing listings and revenue-sharing arrangements. Key obligations include VerticalNet's provision of its Medical Product Listings to Neoforma for exclusive use on Neoforma Plan, Shop, and Auction, as well as Neoforma's listing of these products in a consistent look-and-feel. In return, Neoforma grants VerticalNet an exclusive license to use the listings, subject to terms and conditions. Financial terms include revenue-sharing arrangements, with percentages not specified but implied through the context. The agreement is for an initial term, with automatic renewal provisions.

summary: Network 1 Financial Corporation and USIO, INC. enter into a contract for an ISO program, where USIO acts as the service provider to customers of Network 1. The purpose of the agreement is to establish the terms and conditions under which USIO will provide services to Network 1's customers. Key obligations include USIO's responsibility to obtain merchant applications, sell or lease equipment and products, and receive compensation for its services. Network 1 agrees to pay USIO a fee based on surplus funding after costs, as outlined in Exhibit A. The agreement has a term of one hundred eighty days, which will automatically renew for successive one-year terms unless terminated by either party with thirty days' written notice. Termination can occur due to default, insolvency, bankruptcy, or other specified causes. Financial terms include an Exit Fee of $250,000 and payments made on or before the 25th of each calendar month.
